sections.heading: Philadelphia Received Veteran Center Sasha Kaun with Cash
sections.body: On July 15, 2016, Cleveland traded center Sasha Kaun and cash considerations to Philadelphia for draft rights to Chukwudiebere Maduabum, a second-round pick from 2011 who had not established an NBA career. Kaun was a former Kansas national champion whose rights Cleveland had held for years before bringing him over from Russia in 2015. He appeared briefly for the Cavaliers during their 2015-16 championship season but had a small role behind their principal big men. Philadelphia was in an extended rebuilding period and could take on a veteran contract without demanding an immediate starter. Cleveland wanted another international rights asset and a different salary arrangement rather than an NBA rotation player from the 76ers.

sections.heading: Neither New Arrival Delivered a Fresh NBA Season
sections.body: Kaun did not play regular-season NBA games for Philadelphia following the exchange. His NBA playing record remained the twenty-five appearances he had made for Cleveland during the prior season, and those cannot be carried over as 76ers games. Philadelphia waived him as it adjusted the roster for the 2016-17 campaign. Maduabum, meanwhile, continued his professional career away from the NBA, and his draft rights did not convert into Cavaliers game appearances. These outcomes make the inherited B- grades for each team more about contractual flexibility and speculative rights than actual player performance. Neither side acquired the kind of scoring, rebounding or sustained bench play ordinarily associated with a headline trade. The transaction is useful primarily for tracing two players whose NBA rights changed without producing significant new NBA minutes.

sections.heading: The Cash and Rights Were the Meaningful Considerations
sections.body: The accompanying cash went to Philadelphia, while Cleveland received Maduabum’s rights. The amount of cash is not specified in the canonical record and should not be invented. Philadelphia obtained an economic return along with the opportunity to assess Kaun, and Cleveland shifted the center while preserving a future signing option for a prospect. These are legitimate tools of roster management, yet neither produced a long-term starting center or guard. The inherited Slight 76ers Edge classification sits beside equal B- grades. This is not an evidence-based claim of a large difference in NBA production; it is a slight preference in a minor rights and contract exchange. Cleveland’s 2016 title should not be attributed to its incoming prospect, who never played for that championship roster after this deal.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Slight 76ers Edge with inherited B- grades for both clubs. Philadelphia received Sasha Kaun and cash, but Kaun never appeared in a 76ers regular-season game. Cleveland obtained Chukwudiebere Maduabum’s rights without a subsequent Cavaliers NBA appearance. The small deal primarily shifted contract and international rights options.

sections.heading: Portland Purchased the Draft Rights to Jake Layman
sections.body: On June 23, 2016, Portland acquired the draft rights to Maryland forward Jake Layman, selected by Orlando at No. 47 in the NBA draft. The Magic received a future 2019 second-round choice and $1.2 million in cash. The second-rounder was eventually associated with No. 56 in 2019 and guard Jaylen Hands. Portland had identified Layman as a potential floor-spacing forward who could develop behind its established perimeter scorers. Orlando preferred two future resources rather than keeping the newly drafted prospect. This was not a midseason trade of signed rotation players and did not deliver a first-round selection to either club. The cash amount is recorded in the inherited transaction and should be treated as separate from the draft right. The two teams were valuing a present rookie prospect and a future pick differently.

sections.heading: Layman Developed Into a Useful Portland Reserve
sections.body: Layman played 35 games for the Trail Blazers during 2016-17, appearing only in limited minutes as a rookie. His opportunity expanded over subsequent seasons. In 2018-19 he played 71 regular-season games, made 33 starts and averaged 7.6 points while giving Portland athletic finishing and shooting from the forward position. Those are meaningful direct NBA contributions from the No. 47 rights purchase, even though Layman never became the main star alongside Damian Lillard and CJ McCollum. Portland reached the Western Conference Finals in 2019 with Layman available as a rotation piece. The inherited C+ Blazers grade reflects the multi-season development return rather than his first year alone. His later Minnesota games belong to another club and do not inflate Portland’s accounting.

sections.heading: The Magic Received Money and a Later Second-Round Asset
sections.body: Orlando obtained $1.2 million cash immediately and a 2019 second-rounder that ultimately became No. 56, tied to Jaylen Hands. The tradeable rights or selection had value, but the eventual NBA careers of players acquired through later movements of that pick are not automatically Orlando games. Its inherited C+ grade equals Portland, reflecting that cash and a future selection can be a fair return for a second-round prospect before his development is known. The Blazers got more directly observable playing minutes when Layman became a regular rotation forward; the Magic gained earlier financial resources and delayed draft flexibility. Neither side acquired a new All-Star, and the Even Trade designation recognizes two modest strategies rather than insisting both teams realized identical on-court statistics. The distinction between the 2016 No. 47 player and the 2019 No. 56 draft selection matters to the chronology.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Even Trade under C+ grades for both clubs. Portland gained Jake Layman’s No. 47 draft rights, and Layman later appeared in 71 games with 33 starts at 7.6 points in 2018-19. Orlando acquired $1.2 million and the 2019 No. 56 second-round pick associated with Jaylen Hands.

sections.heading: Cleveland Took Mike Dunleavy for Two International Rights
sections.body: On July 7, 2016, Chicago traded veteran forward Mike Dunleavy Jr. to Cleveland, receiving draft rights to Albert Miralles. The Cavaliers also obtained rights to Russian forward Vladimir Veremeenko from Chicago in the agreement. The Bulls were creating roster and salary flexibility after signing Dwyane Wade and adding Rajon Rondo that summer, while the defending champion Cavaliers wanted another experienced outside shooter. Dunleavy had established himself as a reliable veteran scoring wing across several NBA stops and could potentially stretch the floor around LeBron James. Both draft-rights assets came from international prospects who had not built NBA regular-season careers for their previous rights holders. The trade did not include a first-round pick, and those draft rights should not be mistaken for active NBA players joining Chicago in July.

sections.heading: Dunleavy Played a Brief Cleveland Stint Before Another Trade
sections.body: Dunleavy appeared in 23 Cavaliers games in 2016-17, scoring 4.6 points per game in a limited reserve role. He was not a full-time Cleveland starter and did not remain with the franchise through its entire postseason campaign. In January 2017, Cleveland sent him to Atlanta as part of a separate trade for Kyle Korver. Thus Dunleavy’s later Hawks appearances do not belong to the original Cavaliers return, and Korver’s contribution must be evaluated as part of a different multi-asset transaction rather than assigned solely to the Bulls trade. Cleveland’s B+ inherited grade is generous for the initial short stint but may incorporate the veteran’s usefulness as a subsequent exchange asset. The clear direct court return from Chicago’s July transaction was twenty-three regular-season reserve appearances.

sections.heading: Chicago Received Rights Without Immediate NBA Games
sections.body: Miralles was a Spanish big man originally selected in the second round years earlier. After the trade, he did not arrive in Chicago to contribute NBA regular-season minutes. The Bulls received draft-right optionality and reduced their commitment to a veteran forward while retooling their roster. Chicago’s C+ grade can recognize cap and roster flexibility, but the rights did not become a new immediate starting player. The Cavaliers Win verdict and higher B+ assessment are consistent with Cleveland at least using Dunleavy in games and later including him in another roster move, even if his on-court role fell short of the original hoped-for shooting specialist. Veremeenko’s international career cannot be credited as Cavaliers NBA points either. The transaction exemplifies NBA teams using historical draft rights to complete comparatively small salary-driven veteran moves.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Cavaliers Win. Cleveland receives B+ for Mike Dunleavy Jr. and Vladimir Veremeenko rights; Dunleavy played 23 Cavaliers games at 4.6 points before being traded again. Chicago earns C+ for Albert Miralles rights and roster flexibility but received no incoming player who produced Bulls regular-season minutes.

sections.heading: Denver Collected Two Guards, Two Picks and Cash for Randy Foye
sections.body: On February 18, 2016, Denver traded veteran guard Randy Foye to the Oklahoma City Thunder. The Nuggets obtained D.J. Augustin, forward Steve Novak, two 2016 second-round draft selections and cash. One pick was protected through Nos. 56-60 and eventually identified as No. 53 Petr Cornelie; the other became No. 56 Daniel Hamilton. Oklahoma City wanted a guard who could fit around Russell Westbrook and Kevin Durant during a Western Conference title push, while Denver chose both immediate backup playmaking and multiple development opportunities. This was a substantially larger return than a simple Foye-for-Augustin swap. Both draft selections and the cash were genuine parts of the historical agreement, and the protective condition on one pick should remain distinct from the separate unprotected selection.

sections.heading: Augustin Supplied Needed Bench Playmaking
sections.body: Augustin joined a younger Nuggets backcourt and had more opportunity to handle the ball than he did behind Westbrook in Oklahoma City. In 28 Denver games after the swap, he provided double-digit scoring and several assists per appearance while working in a mostly reserve role. His quickness and shooting helped a team still developing Emmanuel Mudiay and other guards. Novak was another experienced offensive reserve, although his larger contribution to the transaction was the ability to adjust the roster rather than high-volume minutes as a new Nuggets starter. The two second-round picks widened Denver’s future draft options even though both prospects followed their own developmental paths. The Nuggets A+ inherited grade evaluates this broad combination of resources; Augustin alone was not a long-term Denver franchise centerpiece, and his later Orlando seasons belong elsewhere.

sections.heading: Foye Had a Short Thunder Scoring Role
sections.body: Foye appeared in 27 Oklahoma City regular-season games after the trade, averaging roughly six points and providing perimeter depth in a rotation dominated by Westbrook, Durant and other established contributors. He was a supporting guard, not the player whose scoring carried the club into the Western Conference Finals. His professional experience and shooting made sense for a team trying to strengthen the bench without changing its core, but he did not produce a long multi-year Thunder tenure. Oklahoma City’s B grade therefore reflects an immediate veteran playoff option, while Denver’s A+ rewards Augustin, Novak, cash and two future second-round selections. The breadth of Denver’s return is the clearest difference in the original trade even if neither incoming prospect ultimately became an NBA All-Star for the Nuggets.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Nuggets Win. Denver receives A+ for D.J. Augustin, Steve Novak, cash and two 2016 second-round picks tied to No. 53 Petr Cornelie and No. 56 Daniel Hamilton. Oklahoma City earns B for Randy Foye, who played 27 late-season games as a supporting guard during the Thunder’s 2016 playoff run.

sections.heading: Dallas Acquired Former Lottery Center Nerlens Noel at the Deadline
sections.body: On February 23, 2017, Philadelphia traded young center Nerlens Noel to Dallas. The 76ers received wing Justin Anderson, veteran center Andrew Bogut and conditional future draft picks. The principal 2017 condition involved a first-rounder protected through No. 18 that instead became second-round consideration; the inherited record also identifies a protected 2020 second. Those selections were eventually associated with No. 39 Jawun Evans in 2017 and No. 48 Nico Mannion in 2020, although their subsequent rights chains require independent attribution. Dallas wanted a mobile rim protector to evaluate next to its developing guards, while Philadelphia was reallocating frontcourt minutes around Joel Embiid and its other recent lottery selections. The bargain involved real draft conditions, not only a player swap.

sections.heading: Noel Supplied a Useful but Incomplete Mavericks Trial
sections.body: Noel played 22 Dallas regular-season games after the 2017 deadline, starting 12 and averaging about 8.5 points and 6.8 rebounds with active rim protection. Dallas could examine his athleticism and finishing, but his restricted free agency the next summer complicated the franchise’s ability to lock in the arrangement. In 2017-18 his Mavericks role shrank amid injury and playing-time disputes, and he eventually departed for Oklahoma City. The inherited C+ grade accounts for a promising frontcourt experiment that never became a long-term starting-center foundation. Noel’s later rebounding and shot blocking with the Thunder and Knicks must not be credited to Dallas. The first partial season offered encouraging actual play, yet the overall value fell short of what the Mavericks might have envisioned for a former high lottery choice.

sections.heading: Philadelphia Retained a Young Wing and Draft Flexibility
sections.body: Anderson brought the 76ers a younger defensive wing, playing regular minutes during the rest of 2016-17 and returning the following season. Bogut, an experienced championship center acquired principally as salary-matching consideration, did not become a long-term Philadelphia rotation player. The protected draft package gave the Sixers additional assets to select or exchange as they rebuilt around their young stars. Philadelphia’s inherited B grade is numerically higher than Dallas’s C+, even though the original verdict reads Slight Mavericks Edge. That conflict deserves its own grading review rather than a silent rewrite; the factual comparison is a short Noel trial against Anderson and conditional pick value. The 2017 and 2020 draft-right outcomes need to be traced separately instead of treating all named picks as full Philadelphia NBA playing careers.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Slight Mavericks Edge in the inherited winner label, despite grades of Dallas C+ and Philadelphia B. Dallas acquired Nerlens Noel for a 22-game initial center trial, while Philadelphia received Justin Anderson, Andrew Bogut and conditional draft selections associated with 2017 No. 39 Jawun Evans and 2020 No. 48 Nico Mannion. The contradictory winner and grades warrant a separate audit.

sections.heading: Brooklyn Took Dante Cunningham for a Young Guard
sections.body: On February 8, 2018, the Brooklyn Nets acquired veteran forward Dante Cunningham from the New Orleans Pelicans. New Orleans received shooting guard Rashad Vaughn. The transaction was a direct swap of two perimeter and frontcourt reserves at the deadline, not a first-round pick or cash deal. Cunningham was a long-serving defensive forward who had played with New Orleans since 2014 and could guard several positions without using many possessions. Vaughn was a former first-round selection still trying to establish a reliable offensive role after beginning his NBA career with Milwaukee. Brooklyn was giving its young guards more space while adding experienced size; New Orleans wanted a chance to examine a younger perimeter player. The date and terms are consistent across the teams’ historical transaction ledgers.

sections.heading: Cunningham Appeared in Brooklyn’s Rotation
sections.body: Cunningham joined a Nets club outside the playoff race and was asked to provide defense and physical rebounding rather than star-level scoring. He appeared in 22 regular-season games for Brooklyn after the trade, filling small-forward and power-forward roles as a veteran substitute. That was a real on-court return even if he did not sign a long-term deal with the Nets afterward. Cunningham had been a more frequent starter with the Pelicans in earlier years, but Brooklyn did not obtain all those prior New Orleans minutes when it acquired him in February. The Nets C inherited grade reflects the limited length and role of this partial season rather than a complete absence of player production. His subsequent NBA career with other franchises belongs to different agreements.

sections.heading: Vaughn Was a Short-Term Pelicans Experiment
sections.body: Vaughn had struggled to carve out sustained NBA playing time in Milwaukee and had already been traded to Brooklyn earlier in February. New Orleans acquired him as a potential offensive guard prospect, but did not receive the stable scoring role that would have justified a premium future pick. His Pelicans period was short, and he did not become a lasting member of their main rotation. The franchise C grade equals Brooklyn, while the inherited Slight Pelicans Edge label is a narrow judgment about exploring upside in a younger player. It is not a finding that Vaughn supplied more actual Pelicans regular-season minutes than Cunningham contributed to Brooklyn. Neither side surrendered a first-rounder or landed a clear long-term starter, making the exchange one of the smaller moves of the 2018 deadline.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Slight Pelicans Edge in the inherited classification, with C grades for both teams. New Orleans acquired guard Rashad Vaughn for a brief evaluation, while Brooklyn obtained Dante Cunningham, who appeared in 22 Nets games after the February 2018 deadline. Neither side acquired a new franchise-leading scorer.

sections.heading: Dallas Received International Rights and Cash for Motley
sections.body: On July 22, 2018, the Dallas Mavericks traded young forward Johnathan Motley and the NBA draft rights to Lithuanian guard Renaldas Seibutis to the Los Angeles Clippers. Dallas obtained rights to Maarty Leunen and $50,000 in cash. Motley had joined Dallas as an undrafted rookie and earned some NBA opportunities along with developmental-league playing time. The Clippers were looking for inexpensive frontcourt prospects to evaluate alongside their newly reorganized roster. Dallas preferred future rights flexibility and a small financial payment instead of retaining the forward. Leunen was a former second-round choice who had spent years playing overseas, while Seibutis had been drafted earlier and also had an extended European career. No first-round pick or established NBA starting guard was part of the transaction.

sections.heading: Motley Was a Clippers Developmental Big Rather Than a Star
sections.body: Motley split his Los Angeles tenure between the NBA roster and the development system, providing center and forward depth when injuries and rest affected the available lineup. He had shown energy and scoring around the basket in his Dallas opportunities, but he did not become the Clippers primary frontcourt player. The inherited Clippers B- grade credits the chance to test a young NBA-capable big while receiving additional international rights to Seibutis. Neither acquisition should be given statistical credit for the club’s existing veteran starters. Motley did play additional NBA games after moving to Los Angeles, making the exchange more than a purchase of completely unexercised rights. Yet he remained a role player instead of becoming the kind of dependable starter typically acquired for a high first-round draft selection.

sections.heading: Leunen Rights Did Not Become Mavericks Playing Production
sections.body: Leunen was an experienced European basketball player by 2018, but Dallas did not obtain a Mavericks regular-season NBA career from his rights. The $50,000 payment was the tangible immediate economic component of the Dallas return, supplemented by the option to sign or later exchange an international prospect. That calculation was sensible at the margins of a roster beginning the Luka Dončić era, but it did not deliver an established NBA performer. Dallas B- matches the Clippers B- in the inherited assessment, reflecting two low-cost opportunities with different timelines. The Even Trade label is therefore a way of preserving the original neutral grade, not a claim that Motley and Leunen played equivalent NBA minutes for their receiving teams. The actual professional trajectories were distinctly different.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Even Trade according to the inherited B- grades for Dallas and the Clippers. Los Angeles received Johnathan Motley and Renaldas Seibutis rights, while Dallas obtained Maarty Leunen rights and $50,000. Motley provided the only direct NBA playing minutes for his acquiring team, while Dallas received cash and a speculative rights asset.

sections.heading: Brooklyn Took Dwight Howard in a Major Contract Exchange
sections.body: On July 6, 2018, Brooklyn acquired veteran center Dwight Howard from Charlotte. The Hornets took back Timofey Mozgov, rights to young guard Hamidou Diallo, a future 2021 second-round pick and cash considerations. The second-round choice ultimately was associated with No. 57 Balsa Koprivica. This was primarily a trade of contracts, draft rights and financial obligations rather than a basketball exchange expected to produce a full season of Howard playing for the Nets. Charlotte was clearing Howard from the roster after one productive but complicated year and seeking a different path at center. Brooklyn was willing to manage a veteran deal to improve its longer-term payroll position, while sending out Mozgov and other assets. All components need to be recognized; the outgoing Hornets guard rights and future pick were not fictional footnotes to a straight center-for-center trade.

sections.heading: Howard Was Bought Out Before Playing for Brooklyn
sections.body: Howard had averaged a double-double and played heavy minutes for Charlotte during 2017-18, but none of those Hornets statistics can be assigned to Brooklyn. After the July exchange the Nets negotiated a buyout and waived him before he appeared in a Brooklyn regular-season game. He later signed with Washington, where injuries limited his next season. The Nets B+ inherited grade is therefore not based on Howard becoming a Brooklyn starting center, but on management of salary obligations and future financial freedom. The trade cannot be judged as though Brooklyn acquired the multi-year Orlando All-Star version of Howard. In a traditional player-performance comparison there were no Howard Nets minutes from the agreement, which makes the payroll motive essential to interpreting why a team would accept the veteran contract at all.

sections.heading: Charlotte Held Several Assets But Continued Restructuring
sections.body: Mozgov was a veteran center with a sizable deal who was subsequently moved again rather than serving as a long-term Hornets starter. The Diallo draft rights and future second gave Charlotte other options, while the cash compensated part of the transaction economics. Each later draft-right movement is a separate agreement, and the eventual careers of Diallo and Koprivica should not be credited automatically as Charlotte NBA games. Charlotte C grade reflects uncertain asset returns despite the benefit of moving on from Howard. Brooklyn B+ was higher largely because of its preferred financial outcome, not because Howard outscored Mozgov for his receiving club. This was a rebuilding-era exchange in which neither new center provided a sustained regular-season career for the acquiring team.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Nets Win. Brooklyn earns B+ for the Dwight Howard contract transaction and subsequent buyout, although Howard played no Nets regular-season games. Charlotte receives C for Timofey Mozgov, Hamidou Diallo draft rights, a 2021 No. 57 second-round choice later associated with Balsa Koprivica, and cash. The principal Nets benefit was salary management rather than court production.

sections.heading: Washington Paid a Protected First for Markieff Morris
sections.body: On February 18, 2016, Washington acquired forward Markieff Morris from Phoenix, sending Kris Humphries, DeJuan Blair and a future first-round draft pick protected through the top nine. The choice ultimately conveyed at No. 13 in the 2016 draft, associated with center Georgios Papagiannis. Morris had spent several seasons as a prominent Suns forward but his relationship with the team had soured after an earlier roster reshuffle involving his twin brother. Washington needed another scoring power forward to share the floor with John Wall and Bradley Beal. Phoenix accepted two veterans and a significant draft asset rather than keeping a disgruntled starter. The distinction between the protected No. 13 choice and the player eventually selected is important: the Suns subsequently used the draft rights in other transactions and should not be credited with an entire Papagiannis NBA career.

sections.heading: Morris Became a Starting Forward on a Playoff Team
sections.body: Morris joined the Wizards during the 2015-16 season and quickly became a regular part of their frontcourt. His larger contribution came in 2016-17, when he started throughout a 49-win Washington season and averaged about 14 points and more than six rebounds per game. The Wizards reached the second round and pushed Boston to seven games, with Morris filling an important defensive and offensive role alongside Wall and Beal. He remained in Washington for additional seasons, meaning the acquisition was much more than a six-week rental. The original C+ Wizards grade is conservative compared with his eventual starting role, but it recognizes that the club gave up a real first-round pick. His later Detroit and Los Angeles seasons should not be folded into Washington’s direct return.

sections.heading: Phoenix Received a Pick With Substantial Draft-Day Value
sections.body: Humphries and Blair were experienced interior players but did not give Phoenix a long-running new starting frontcourt. The No. 13 first-round choice, by contrast, was valuable enough to become part of the 2016 draft-night maneuvering that brought another lottery prospect into the Suns system. That pick had genuine value even if the team did not keep the rights to the player originally named at No. 13. Phoenix’s B inherited grade exceeds Washington’s C+, while the canonical verdict says Wizards Win. This winner-and-grade disagreement needs separate source-led regrading rather than silently changing the historical record. The basketball comparison is several Washington starting seasons from Morris versus two incoming reserves and a high draft selection that Phoenix could redeploy. Both sides had meaningful returns on different timelines.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Wizards Win in the inherited verdict, although Phoenix earns B and Washington C+. The Wizards acquired Markieff Morris, an established 2016-17 starting forward, while Phoenix received Kris Humphries, DeJuan Blair and a top-nine-protected first that became No. 13 in 2016. The discrepancy between winner label and grades warrants review.

sections.heading: Detroit Obtained a Conditional Future Second for Jodie Meeks
sections.body: On June 29, 2016, Detroit traded veteran shooting guard Jodie Meeks to Orlando for a conditional 2019 second-round selection. The inherited transaction specifies an unusual condition: the less favorable of the Portland pick and the most favorable of several other selections linked to Cleveland, Orlando and Houston. The eventually identified draft asset became No. 56 in 2019, associated with Jaylen Hands. Detroit wanted to open perimeter rotation and salary flexibility after Meeks had struggled with injuries, while Orlando hoped a veteran shooter could help its offense around emerging frontcourt players. No first-round pick was involved. The conditional mechanics matter because the final 2019 draft number was not predetermined when the clubs agreed in 2016. The trade was made before free agency, making roster planning as important as the immediate basketball exchange.

sections.heading: Meeks Was a Useful Magic Shooter Before Another Injury
sections.body: Meeks entered Orlando with a reputation for outside shooting from earlier Los Angeles and Detroit seasons, though injuries had reduced his availability. In 2016-17 he played 36 regular-season games for the Magic, contributing perimeter offense in a reserve role. He scored more than eight points per game during that partial season and supplied a veteran option behind Orlando’s younger guards. However, further injury prevented him from delivering a full year or another extended Magic tenure. Orlando’s inherited C grade reflects genuine shooting value but limited duration. It should not count his earlier Detroit high-volume shooting seasons as new Orlando production or treat the single stint as a franchise-defining acquisition. The Magic paid with a delayed pick whose final identity depended on other clubs’ draft rights.

sections.heading: The No. 56 Pick Was Detroit’s Future Return
sections.body: Detroit received a future second-round option and flexibility in its guard rotation instead of an immediate incoming player. The condition later matured into the 2019 No. 56 pick associated with UCLA guard Jaylen Hands, a real draft-right asset rather than a nonconveyed promise. Any later movement of Hands’s rights must be separated from Detroit NBA regular-season minutes, because draft-right ownership and a player’s eventual team are not the same thing. The Pistons B+ inherited grade values the asset and the limited cost of moving an injury-affected veteran. Orlando C is lower even though Meeks supplied some usable three-point shooting. From a rebuilding perspective Detroit favored future flexibility, while Orlando accepted a shorter-term floor-spacing gamble. The original Pistons Win verdict reflects those different costs and returns, not an NBA starting player received instantly by Detroit.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Pistons Win. Detroit receives B+ for a conditional 2019 second-round choice eventually associated with No. 56 Jaylen Hands and the flexibility to move Jodie Meeks. Orlando earns C after Meeks played 36 games as a shooting reserve during 2016-17. The incoming Pistons asset was a draft pick, not immediate player production.

sections.heading: Denver Accepted Mo Williams and Cash for Overseas Draft Rights
sections.body: On January 18, 2017, Atlanta transferred veteran guard Mo Williams and cash considerations to Denver. The Hawks received draft rights to Turkish guard Cenk Akyol and a traded-player exception. Williams had been a useful scorer earlier in his career, including an NBA championship season with Cleveland in 2015-16, but by January 2017 his remaining contract was more important to the salary transaction than his ability to contribute a new full Nuggets season. Denver had an opportunity to accept the player contract and financial compensation while exchanging rights it was unlikely to convert into an NBA contributor. Atlanta was rearranging its salary obligations after changes to its veteran backcourt. The transaction did not convey an incoming first-round pick or an established Nuggets starter to the Hawks.

sections.heading: Williams Never Became a Denver Rotation Guard
sections.body: Williams had made his final NBA playing appearances with Cleveland before this Denver transaction and did not emerge as a new Nuggets starter. The franchise instead managed his contract as part of a sequence of roster decisions in the middle of the 2016-17 season. Denver was developing younger players and had established guards available, making a long Williams playing tenure an unlikely reason for the deal. Its inherited A- grade should therefore be read as an assessment of taking cash and the ability to reorganize assets, not as a claim that Williams averaged double figures in Denver. The guard’s earlier Cleveland and Minnesota seasons were legitimate professional achievements but belong to those teams. The absence of Nuggets game totals is a key distinction when reviewing what Denver actually received.

sections.heading: Atlanta Held Akyol Rights and a Trade Exception
sections.body: Akyol had been drafted more than a decade earlier and had spent his professional career outside the NBA. He never became a Hawks regular-season guard after the exchange, so Atlanta’s acquired rights were a speculative international signing option rather than proven immediate playing value. The traded-player exception gave the franchise additional payroll flexibility for a future move, though any later acquisition would have its own asset accounting. Atlanta’s inherited B- grade recognizes those rights and salary tools without inventing an NBA player or a premium draft pick. The canonical Nuggets Win verdict favors the team that obtained Williams’s contract and cash, while the Hawks accepted a narrower long-horizon roster option. Neither side acquired a new star, and the relative value depends more on contractual decisions than box scores.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Nuggets Win in the inherited A- for Denver versus B- for Atlanta assessment. Denver accepted Mo Williams and cash but received no new Williams regular-season playing production. The Hawks obtained Cenk Akyol draft rights and a traded-player exception. This was principally a salary-and-rights exchange rather than a guard-for-guard scoring trade.

sections.heading: Phoenix Took Mike Scott, Akyol Rights and Cash for a Conditional Second
sections.body: On February 23, 2017, Atlanta sent forward Mike Scott, draft rights to Cenk Akyol and cash to Phoenix. The Hawks received a 2017 second-round choice protected through No. 55, a condition that did not convey in the historical transaction ledger. This exchange was part of Atlanta’s continued salary management after other January and February moves, including the earlier transaction that had brought Akyol rights from Denver. Scott was a veteran power forward who had given Atlanta useful reserve shooting in prior seasons but whose 2016-17 role was diminished. Phoenix was willing to take the contract and financial considerations rather than give up a guaranteed selection. The Suns obtained a second international rights option alongside Scott, not a new draft pick.

sections.heading: Scott Did Not Play a New Suns Season
sections.body: Scott had appeared for Atlanta in previous years and became a productive bench scorer for Washington later in his career. Neither period counts as Phoenix playing production from this trade. He did not become a Suns regular-season rotation forward after the February agreement, making the basketball return smaller than the familiar player name might suggest. The franchise received the cash accompanying him and was able to control how it managed the incoming contract. The inherited Suns B grade therefore reflects asset and financial management rather than a claimed twenty-point scoring season from Scott. The trade came during Phoenix’s broader rebuild around young perimeter and frontcourt players, with no expectation that a February reserve acquisition would change the team’s playoff prospects. His eventual time in Washington is a separate free-agent decision.

sections.heading: The Hawks Did Not Receive a Selected Second-Round Prospect
sections.body: Atlanta’s conditional compensation was a second-round pick protected through the top 55 draft positions in 2017. The inherited record says the condition did not activate, leaving no actual selected NBA player for the Hawks to credit to this agreement. The club did gain the ability to redirect Scott’s contract and give other players minutes, but its direct draft return was not a future prospect who later started games. Akyol rights also left the franchise for Phoenix without creating an Atlanta NBA playing career. The Hawks C+ inherited grade recognizes that roster-management benefit while acknowledging the nonconveyed pick. Phoenix’s B is slightly higher because it received cash and two controlled assets at effectively no realized draft cost. This makes the Suns Win result more about avoiding a pick transfer than on-court scoring.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Suns Win. Phoenix earns B for Mike Scott, Cenk Akyol rights and cash considerations, although Scott did not play a Suns regular-season game. Atlanta receives C+ for a top-55-protected 2017 second-round pick that did not convey. Neither side acquired a new NBA starting player from the trade.

sections.heading: The Pacers Acquired Jeremy Evans and International Rights
sections.body: On July 7, 2016, Dallas sent veteran forward Jeremy Evans, NBA draft rights to Emir Preldžić and cash to Indiana. In return the Mavericks acquired rights to Croatian center Stanko Barać. Evans had been known for spectacular athletic plays and his time with Utah, including winning the 2012 NBA Slam Dunk Contest, but had only a small Dallas rotation role in 2015-16. Indiana was exploring an inexpensive wing and forward option without surrendering a current starting player or premium draft pick. Dallas chose a different overseas rights asset while moving an expendable contract. The cash moved with Evans to the Pacers and should not be reversed in the asset accounting. Both international prospects had been drafted years before the exchange and had spent their professional careers away from NBA regular-season rosters.

sections.heading: Evans Did Not Recreate His Utah Role in Indiana
sections.body: Evans was an experienced forward with leaping ability and a history of reserve NBA appearances, but acquiring him did not give the Pacers a new full-season starting power forward. His roster status changed before he could establish a substantial regular-season role in Indiana, and the team already had other options around Paul George and its experienced frontcourt. His earlier Utah dunk highlights and Dallas reserve games should not be treated as a Pacers return from the July 2016 agreement. The Pacers B+ inherited grade can recognize receiving financial consideration plus an NBA-experienced player and rights to Preldžić, but it is generous if measured solely by subsequent Indiana player statistics. Any evaluation should distinguish the assets owned from the points and rebounds actually recorded for their receiving franchise. No long-running Pacers NBA scoring career resulted from this particular agreement.

sections.heading: Dallas Received Barać Rights Without an NBA Arrival
sections.body: Barać had a lengthy professional career abroad but never became a Dallas NBA regular-season center after the trade. The Mavericks therefore gained signing or future-transfer optionality, not immediate basketball production from an incoming seven-footer. Their C- inherited grade reflects the narrow value of that rights claim compared with the cash and two different assets that went to Indiana. The player-right chains behind Preldžić and Barać are part of the deal’s history, but neither career in European leagues can be credited as NBA games for Dallas or Indiana. Indiana’s higher B+ and the Slight Pacers Edge verdict are consistent with receiving more varied assets, even though the direct NBA playing impact of both sides was limited. This was a salary and roster options maneuver during a summer of broader moves for both teams.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Slight Pacers Edge. Indiana earns B+ for Jeremy Evans, Emir Preldžić rights and cash considerations; Evans did not establish a new regular-season starting role for the Pacers. Dallas receives C- for Stanko Barać draft rights, which never became a Mavericks NBA playing career. The return was largely contractual and speculative.

sections.heading: Denver Traded Harris, Hampton and a First for Aaron Gordon
sections.body: At the March 25, 2021 deadline, Denver acquired Aaron Gordon and Gary Clark Jr. from Orlando. The Magic obtained Gary Harris, RJ Hampton and a future first-round selection with top-five protections that eventually matured at No. 25 in 2025, used on Jase Richardson. Denver had established its offense around Nikola Jokić and Jamal Murray but needed a larger defender who could finish at the basket without monopolizing the ball. Gordon had spent years in Orlando as a high-profile lottery forward and wanted to compete in the playoffs. The Magic was rebuilding and preferred younger pieces along with a first-round asset. This was not simply Gordon for Harris; Hampton and the future pick were consequential costs to Denver, and Clark arrived as the other player acquired.

sections.heading: Gordon Became the Defensive Forward on a Championship Team
sections.body: Gordon immediately accepted a different role in Denver, cutting toward the rim, defending larger wings and switching assignments while Jokić handled playmaking. He became a central starter on the 2022-23 Nuggets team that won the franchise’s first NBA championship. His ability to defend multiple frontcourt players and score efficiently without needing the ball gave Denver a missing complementary piece. He remained important during further playoff runs and signed a longer commitment to the club. The Nuggets A+ inherited grade is supported by sustained starting minutes and a title with Gordon as an actual contributor, not by attributing every Jokić achievement solely to the trade. The shorter contributions from Clark should be acknowledged without placing them on the same level as Gordon’s years of impact.

sections.heading: Orlando Received a Guard and Prospect Before Its Later Rebuild
sections.body: Harris brought veteran perimeter defense and shooting to Orlando, while Hampton offered a chance to develop a young backcourt player. The future first-round selection provided another asset that eventually became No. 25 in 2025, associated with Jase Richardson. Those were legitimate returns but did not produce an Orlando champion or a star with Gordon’s specific Denver impact. The Magic B- inherited grade reflects useful experience and future draft flexibility while acknowledging the loss of a physically versatile starter. The team later developed a separate young frontcourt around Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner, but those players were acquired through other decisions and should not be credited to this trade as though they were part of the return. The trade’s direct long-term win belongs to the Denver side.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Nuggets Win. Denver earns A+ for Aaron Gordon and Gary Clark Jr., with Gordon eventually becoming a starting defender on its 2023 championship team. Orlando receives B- for Gary Harris, RJ Hampton and a protected future first-rounder that became No. 25 Jase Richardson in 2025. The championship frontcourt role validates Denver’s choice.

sections.heading: Chicago Used a Sign-and-Trade for DeMar DeRozan
sections.body: On August 11, 2021, Chicago acquired All-Star scorer DeMar DeRozan from San Antonio in a sign-and-trade. The Spurs received Thaddeus Young, Al-Farouq Aminu, a 2022 second-round selection connected to No. 38 Kennedy Chandler, and a protected future first-rounder that eventually became No. 12 Noa Essengue in 2025. The Bulls had already added Lonzo Ball and were trying to assemble a more competitive roster around Zach LaVine and Nikola Vučević. DeRozan was one of the league’s most established midrange shot creators, while San Antonio was moving toward its next young core. The agreement was not a simple swap of shooting guards: Chicago paid with two veteran forwards and multiple valuable draft selections. Both pick chains need to be accounted for separately from any additional subsequent rights trades.

sections.heading: DeRozan Quickly Delivered All-NBA-Level Chicago Scoring
sections.body: DeRozan immediately became Chicago’s leading late-game scorer. In 2021-22 he averaged 27.9 points and 4.9 assists over 76 games, earned All-NBA Second Team recognition and helped lead the Bulls to the postseason for the first time since 2017. He repeatedly created difficult midrange shots late in games and provided a reliable offensive option when the team’s younger guards struggled. His production remained above twenty points per game in multiple subsequent Chicago seasons, giving the franchise more than one short rental. The inherited A grade reflects scoring and leadership that clearly came from the acquired player, not from earlier Raptors or Spurs statistics imported into the Bulls ledger. The franchise did not become a title favorite solely through the trade, but it obtained a dependable veteran centerpiece with a major role in an improved regular-season offense.

sections.heading: San Antonio Collected Draft Assets for the Next Roster Cycle
sections.body: Young and Aminu were experienced forwards whose contracts offered the Spurs several possible roster approaches. San Antonio also received a second-round pick in 2022 and a protected future first that eventually became a 2025 lottery selection. A future No. 12 pick represented genuine rebuilding capital, and San Antonio’s C inherited grade may appear conservative given that payoff. However, the complete NBA playing careers of Kennedy Chandler and Noa Essengue should not be assigned to the Spurs without establishing every subsequent rights movement. The direct trade moved a high-level veteran scorer out of San Antonio before another draft-led rebuild, while giving the team several compensating assets. Chicago’s higher A grade rewards years of immediately measurable All-NBA scoring. The sides had very different competitive priorities in August 2021.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Bulls Win. Chicago earns A for DeMar DeRozan, who averaged 27.9 points during his first Chicago season and earned All-NBA recognition. San Antonio gets C for Thaddeus Young, Al-Farouq Aminu, a 2022 second-round asset tied to No. 38 Kennedy Chandler and a protected first that later became No. 12 Noa Essengue in 2025.

sections.heading: Portland Acquired Norman Powell for Two Scoring Wings
sections.body: On March 25, 2021, Portland traded Gary Trent Jr. and Rodney Hood to Toronto for Norman Powell. The Trail Blazers wanted another established perimeter scorer to accompany Damian Lillard and CJ McCollum in a playoff push. Powell had played an important role on the Raptors’ 2019 championship team and had expanded into a higher-scoring offensive guard. Toronto accepted the chance to develop Trent while adding veteran Hood, whose injury history had constrained his recent output. The transaction contained no future first-round draft pick or cash in the inherited canonical record. Both outgoing Blazers had already played regular NBA minutes, making this a genuine reshuffling of wing rotation roles rather than a draft-night rights transaction. The different career trajectories of Powell and Trent after the deal form the core of its hindsight assessment.

sections.heading: Powell Provided High-Volume Shooting Before Moving On
sections.body: Powell joined Portland for the closing weeks of the 2020-21 regular season and became an immediate starting perimeter option. He scored more than seventeen points per game during his Blazers stretch while combining three-point shooting with the ability to attack off the dribble. Powell returned in 2021-22 before being traded again to the Los Angeles Clippers in a separate deal. That gave Portland a useful veteran but not a long-lasting fixture in its main backcourt. Its inherited C grade reflects the limited length and lack of deep postseason improvement, rather than claiming Powell failed to contribute. His later strong Clippers seasons cannot be counted as Trail Blazers scoring after he had departed. At the moment of the acquisition he fit the club’s near-term needs, but the later roster transition shortened the realized reward.

sections.heading: Trent Became a Toronto Scoring Starter
sections.body: Trent took on a larger offensive role with Toronto, emerging as a regular starting guard and perimeter scorer. During the 2021-22 season he averaged 18.3 points while starting 69 games, supporting a Raptors team that returned to the playoffs. Hood supplied a shorter veteran forward stint and did not become the principal Toronto payoff. Trent’s development into a young high-volume guard gave the Raptors a more durable asset than Powell’s brief Portland tenure, and Toronto’s B+ inherited grade exceeds the Blazers C. The historical verdict, however, labels the deal Slight Blazers Edge, a conflict between the numerical grades and the player outcomes. A proper canonical regrade should address that contradiction instead of disguising it in the editorial. The direct NBA evidence points to a long Toronto Trent tenure versus a shorter Powell stop in Portland.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Slight Blazers Edge is the inherited verdict, despite grades of Portland C and Toronto B+. Portland acquired Norman Powell for a productive but shorter stay. Toronto received Gary Trent Jr., who averaged 18.3 points with 69 starts in 2021-22, plus Rodney Hood. The winner and grades require a separate reconciliation.

sections.heading: Charlotte Acquired Center Mason Plumlee and JT Thor Rights
sections.body: On August 6, 2021, Charlotte acquired veteran center Mason Plumlee and the draft rights to Auburn forward J.T. Thor from Detroit. The Pistons received the rights to Serbian center Balsa Koprivica, chosen late in the second round. Charlotte needed an experienced screening and passing center after a season of rotation changes, and Plumlee had started much of the preceding season in Detroit. The deal also brought Charlotte another young forward prospect, not only the veteran contract. Detroit was adjusting its frontcourt around younger players and accepted a different second-round developmental right. The Bobcats/Hornets franchise and Detroit transaction ledgers both identify the unusual combination of an active NBA center and two drafted prospect rights. No first-round selection was involved.

sections.heading: Plumlee Became a Regular Starting Hornets Center
sections.body: Plumlee started 73 Charlotte games in 2021-22, averaging 6.5 points, 7.7 rebounds and 3.1 assists. He helped move the ball from the high post and rebound for a team emphasizing speed around LaMelo Ball. The following season he remained productive until the franchise traded him to the Clippers at the 2023 deadline. He was never expected to become the Hornets’ leading scorer, but his starting experience and passing gave a younger lineup more offensive structure. Charlotte’s B inherited grade reflects more than a temporary minimum-contract backup: the team obtained a reliable starting center who played consistent minutes. Thor developed separately as a young forward, offering another chance at a long-term roster contributor. The total Charlotte return included two distinct players with different timelines.

sections.heading: Detroit Obtained an Unproven International Prospect Right
sections.body: Koprivica was a 2021 second-round selection who had played at Florida State and later pursued professional opportunities outside the NBA. Detroit received his rights, but no immediate veteran center minutes in return from Charlotte. Its inherited C+ grade can recognize the right to develop or move the prospect, along with the ability to adjust the center rotation around its rebuilding priorities. It should not pretend Koprivica started a full Pistons NBA season after the exchange, because he did not establish such a tenure. Charlotte’s stronger direct return was Plumlee’s immediate 73 starts and years of supporting center work, while Detroit accepted speculative future options. The transaction became a useful low-cost means of obtaining real center play for Charlotte without losing a premium draft pick.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Charlotte Win. The Hornets earn B after receiving Mason Plumlee, who made 73 starts with 7.7 rebounds and 3.1 assists in 2021-22, along with J.T. Thor rights. Detroit receives C+ for Balsa Koprivica rights, an international/developmental asset that did not immediately produce Pistons NBA center minutes.

sections.heading: Chicago Signed Lonzo Ball Through a Multi-Asset Swap
sections.body: In August 2021, Chicago acquired point guard Lonzo Ball from New Orleans in a sign-and-trade. The Pelicans received veteran guards Tomas Satoransky and Garrett Temple, cash considerations and a future 2024 second-round pick that ultimately became No. 41 Adem Bona. Chicago hoped Ball’s passing, defense and spot-up shooting could help a roster featuring Zach LaVine and newly acquired veterans. New Orleans was changing its backcourt plans around Zion Williamson and Brandon Ingram, and Ball had a stronger opportunity to become a starting guard elsewhere. The trade was not a simple free-agent signing without outgoing player assets. Temple, Satoransky, cash and the second-round choice were all identifiable consideration for the Pelicans. The historical transaction terms need to be considered alongside Ball’s subsequent availability.

sections.heading: Ball Provided Forty-Seven Games of Strong Perimeter Defense
sections.body: Ball played 35 games for Chicago during 2021-22, all starts, averaging 13.0 points, 5.4 rebounds and 5.1 assists while shooting 42.3 percent on threes. The Bulls started the season strongly, and his defense and quick passing helped link their perimeter scorers. However, a knee injury ended his 2021-22 campaign in January, and he missed the next two full NBA seasons while recovering. Ball eventually returned, but the prolonged absence dramatically affected the expected value of the acquisition. Chicago’s C+ inherited grade reflects a bright initial stint overshadowed by lost seasons on a substantial contract. It would be misleading either to deny the impressive 35-game contribution or to treat the early defense and shooting as several completed healthy Bulls seasons. The health disruption is central to the hindsight verdict.

sections.heading: New Orleans Secured Other Options While Chicago Carried the Risk
sections.body: Satoransky and Temple provided veteran backcourt and wing options, and the Pelicans also obtained cash and a future second-round selection. The pick later connected to No. 41 Adem Bona through subsequent draft movements, creating an additional asset beyond the two player contracts. Neither veteran guard became a replacement All-Star, yet New Orleans avoided committing to Ball’s uncertain health and had more financial and roster flexibility. Its inherited B grade exceeds Chicago’s C+ because the expected long-term upside of the Bulls acquisition was limited by his severe injury absence. The slight Pelicans edge should not be portrayed as a victory derived from Temple averaging huge new scoring numbers; the value lay in depth, the draft pick and the retained options. Ball’s earlier Lakers and Pelicans statistics are not Bulls performance.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Slight Pelicans Edge. New Orleans receives B for Tomas Satoransky, Garrett Temple, cash and a future second eventually tied to 2024 No. 41 Adem Bona. Chicago gets C+ for Lonzo Ball, who averaged 13.0 points with 42.3% three-point shooting in 35 starts before a knee injury interrupted his tenure for two full seasons.

sections.heading: Brooklyn Took Greg Monroe and a Second for Cash
sections.body: On February 7, 2019, Toronto sent veteran center Greg Monroe and a 2021 second-round draft selection to Brooklyn for cash considerations. The choice eventually became No. 37 in 2021, tied to Auburn forward J.T. Thor. Toronto was making room and reducing payroll costs while assembling the roster that would win the NBA championship that June. Monroe had played a limited Raptors reserve role and did not fit the club’s playoff rotation plans once Marc Gasol arrived in a separate deal. Brooklyn could take a contract to obtain a future second-round asset, even without using the center on the floor. The transaction was a player-plus-pick exchange for financial compensation, not an acquisition of a long-term Nets starting center.

sections.heading: Monroe Never Played a Nets Regular-Season Game
sections.body: Brooklyn waived Monroe shortly after acquiring him, and he never appeared in a regular-season game for the franchise as part of this agreement. His earlier Detroit and Milwaukee years were genuine NBA accomplishments, but they have no bearing on Nets playing production from the February 2019 trade. The Nets nevertheless obtained a draft selection with future value and the option to hold or move the rights when the 2021 draft arrived. Brooklyn B+ in the inherited grading reflects collecting a second-round choice for accepting a short-lived veteran contract. The club did not need Monroe to play thirty minutes a night to generate that financial return. The distinction between a completed draft-right transaction and the absence of center playing minutes is central to evaluating the outcome.

sections.heading: Toronto Paid Cash to Create Roster Flexibility
sections.body: The Raptors received no new player or first-round draft choice from Brooklyn. The cash and salary movement gave Toronto more space to optimize a championship-contending roster after other February deadline moves. Its inherited C grade recognizes a reasonable financial decision but discounts the second-round pick surrendered. The eventual No. 37 selection became associated with J.T. Thor, yet Thor’s later NBA games were with Charlotte rather than Brooklyn and should not be credited as Brooklyn court production. The Nets controlled a valuable draft asset, while Toronto addressed immediate payroll and rotation priorities. This is a clear example of teams exchanging short-term flexibility for longer-horizon pick potential, and the winner should be understood in that context rather than as a Monroe-for-cash statistical comparison.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Nets Win. Brooklyn earns B+ after accepting Greg Monroe’s contract and obtaining a future second-round pick that became No. 37 J.T. Thor in 2021, even though Monroe played no Nets games. Toronto receives C for cash and roster flexibility during its 2019 championship season. The draft asset created the longer-term Nets advantage.

sections.heading: Washington Purchased Rights to Admiral Schofield with Cash Consideration
sections.body: At the 2019 NBA draft, Philadelphia selected Tennessee forward Admiral Schofield with the No. 42 choice, then transferred his draft rights and veteran wing Jonathon Simmons to Washington for $2 million cash. The dated transaction ledgers describe the two incoming Washington assets and the economic compensation sent to Philadelphia. Schofield had been an accomplished college scorer and rebounder, while Simmons had previously been a Spurs and Magic rotation wing before his opportunities narrowed. The Wizards were seeking younger, inexpensive talent during an offseason centered on reorganizing the roster around Bradley Beal and John Wall’s injury absence. Philadelphia was converting a second-round draft selection and an expendable veteran contract into a cash payment rather than retaining either player as part of its playoff rotation.

sections.heading: Schofield Received an Immediate Wizards Rookie Opportunity
sections.body: Schofield appeared in 33 Washington regular-season games during 2019-20 and started two, averaging 3.0 points and 1.4 rebounds in limited minutes. That was a direct NBA playing return from the purchased second-round right, though it did not make him a long-term starting forward. Simmons never became an equally important Washington scoring option, and the team waived him before he established a regular role. The Wizards A inherited grade is unusually high for the realized Schofield minutes, but it reflects purchasing a rookie draft opportunity and potential without surrendering a future first-round selection. The rookie still entered an NBA lineup rather than leaving his draft rights unused overseas. He later played for Orlando, whose statistics should not be attributed to Washington’s player development outcome.

sections.heading: Philadelphia Received Money, Not Another Draft Selection
sections.body: The 76ers obtained $2 million for their second-round rights and Simmons contract, supplying real financial flexibility without adding a new player. Cash receipts can help a franchise operate within tax and roster constraints, but they do not produce NBA box scores or a direct first-round asset. Philadelphia C- recognizes that limitation, while Washington A gives weight to a young player it could examine in NBA games. Schofield’s later tenure did not become a star-level return, so the enormous grade gap reflects the original speculative promise more than a franchise-transforming hindsight outcome. Both teams had different reasons for making the trade, and an informed assessment should separate immediate cash savings from the basketball contribution of a rookie forward. The transaction was not a direct Simmons-for-Schofield player swap; both moved in the same direction to Washington.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Wizards Win. Washington receives A for Admiral Schofield’s No. 42 draft rights and Jonathon Simmons, with Schofield playing 33 NBA games during his rookie season. Philadelphia earns C- for $2 million in cash. Washington obtained a player-development opportunity, though Schofield did not become a long-term starting star.

sections.heading: Detroit Exchanged Tony Bradley for Zhaire Smith
sections.body: On November 23, 2020, Philadelphia traded guard-forward Zhaire Smith to Detroit for center Tony Bradley. The 76ers had selected Smith in a 2018 draft-night trade but his early NBA development was derailed by a serious allergic reaction and additional health problems. Detroit was willing to evaluate a still-young athletic wing in exchange for an experienced reserve center. Philadelphia needed interior depth behind Joel Embiid while adjusting its roster for a new coaching staff led by Doc Rivers. No future first-round pick or cash accompanied the direct player swap. It was a late offseason move designed to adjust two different positions, rather than a transaction to acquire a new leading perimeter scorer or a cornerstone big man.

sections.heading: Bradley Supplied Short-Term Center Minutes to Philadelphia
sections.body: Bradley played 20 regular-season 76ers games in 2020-21, with a small number of starts when the rotation needed interior coverage. He scored efficiently near the rim and provided rebounding without demanding many offensive touches. Philadelphia later moved him to Oklahoma City in a separate March 2021 multi-team agreement, meaning his stay lasted only part of the season. The inherited Philadelphia C grade can be justified by reserve center availability at a time when the club was competing for the top of the Eastern Conference standings. His later NBA rebounds with other organizations do not become additional Philadelphia production. The trade did not suddenly deliver a new all-defense center, but it acquired a healthy, usable player who could cover minutes when Embiid rested or missed time.

sections.heading: Smith Never Played a Pistons Regular-Season Game
sections.body: Detroit waived Smith soon after the November trade, and he did not make a regular-season appearance for the Pistons. His NBA playing career to that point had consisted of brief Philadelphia stretches after major health difficulties. Detroit’s C inherited grade is therefore mostly a valuation of the chance to assess a former first-round prospect and create roster flexibility, rather than actual new Pistons scoring. Philadelphia received the only direct on-court games from this agreement. The original 76ers Win label conflicts with equal C grades, making this a slight positional preference instead of a numeric grade victory. Neither club surrendered a premium draft pick in the 2020 transaction, and the most meaningful outcome was Bradley’s short 76ers reserve tenure versus Smith’s unconverted Pistons opportunity.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: 76ers Win with equal inherited C grades. Philadelphia received Tony Bradley, who supplied twenty regular-season appearances and center depth before a separate 2021 move. Detroit acquired former first-rounder Zhaire Smith but waived him without any Pistons NBA games. Neither side received a lasting new starter.

sections.heading: Brooklyn Took Jevon Carter and a First-Round Prospect for Shamet
sections.body: On August 6, 2021, Brooklyn traded guard Landry Shamet to the Phoenix Suns. The Nets received defensive point guard Jevon Carter and draft rights to No. 29 Day’Ron Sharpe, a North Carolina center selected in the 2021 first round. Phoenix had reached the NBA Finals the preceding season and wanted another established shooter alongside Chris Paul and Devin Booker. Brooklyn was assembling a title contender around Kevin Durant, James Harden and Kyrie Irving but also sought younger depth and salary options. The agreement was a player-plus-draft-right transaction, not simply Carter for Shamet. Sharpe represented a genuine late-first-round developmental opportunity for a Nets frontcourt that needed additional rebounding. Both teams’ records agree on the player and rights movements.

sections.heading: Sharpe Became a Nets Reserve Big as Carter Moved On
sections.body: Sharpe joined Brooklyn as a young center with the potential to rebound and finish near the basket. He appeared in 32 games as a rookie in 2021-22, then took on a larger reserve role in subsequent seasons. His value grew beyond the immediate first-year output as the Nets changed their frontcourt roster. Carter played only 46 Nets games before being waived in February 2022 and later signed by Milwaukee, so he was a short-term guard return rather than a long-tenured Brooklyn defensive specialist. The inherited Nets C grade reflects mixed immediate results but a genuine first-round draft prospect. It would be inaccurate to describe Carter as a multi-season mainstay, just as it would be misleading to count all of Sharpe’s future development as completed during his rookie season. The two incoming assets had notably different trajectories.

sections.heading: Phoenix Obtained a Rotation Shooter but Paid a Pick
sections.body: Shamet played a regular Suns perimeter role in 2021-22, making three-point shots and handling occasional extra ball movement when the main guards rested. He stayed with the franchise for two seasons before a separate trade, giving Phoenix more immediate NBA shooting than Carter supplied Brooklyn. However, the Suns surrendered the chance to develop Sharpe at No. 29. The inherited Slight Suns Edge with equal C grades treats Shamet’s veteran fit as marginally more valuable than Brooklyn’s younger center option and brief Carter stint. Both clubs received NBA game contributions, but the longer-horizon case may favor the Nets depending on Sharpe’s eventual career. The source-led evaluation should not overstate either team’s playoff fortunes as the direct result of one supporting-guard trade.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Slight Suns Edge with inherited C grades on both sides. Phoenix obtained Landry Shamet to supplement its shooting rotation; Brooklyn received Jevon Carter and No. 29 Day’Ron Sharpe, who developed into a reserve center after his 2021-22 rookie season. The trade compared present shooting with younger rebounding and draft value.

sections.heading: Charlotte Acquired Veteran Point Guard Brad Wanamaker
sections.body: On March 25, 2021, Charlotte acquired reserve point guard Brad Wanamaker, cash and a top-54-protected 2022 second-round pick from Golden State. The Warriors obtained a 2025 second-round selection with top-55 protection. Both picks ultimately failed to convey under their historical conditions. Charlotte needed experienced guard depth while its young ball handlers dealt with injuries and developmental demands. Wanamaker had played in the NBA with Boston and Golden State and could organize a second unit without being a major scorer. The Warriors were adjusting their reserve backcourt and wanted more flexibility behind Stephen Curry. Because the deal involved two conditional seconds that never became selected players, it is essential not to invent draft-prospect returns for either team. The cash was real consideration to Charlotte, but the most immediate basketball asset was Wanamaker.

sections.heading: Wanamaker Played Fifteen Hornets Games
sections.body: After the agreement, Wanamaker appeared in fifteen Charlotte regular-season contests during the 2020-21 campaign, supplying veteran passing and defense in limited minutes. His scoring was modest, and he did not displace LaMelo Ball or other younger backcourt players when the roster was healthy. The Hornets were competitive for a postseason play-in spot, and Wanamaker provided a contingency option during the closing stretch. He did not become a multi-year Charlotte starting guard, later playing for other franchises. The inherited C Charlotte grade is consistent with a brief but measurable reserve role. His earlier Boston playoff performances and Warriors minutes are not Charlotte production from this particular transaction. The deal made sense as short-term guard insurance rather than a foundational roster investment.

sections.heading: Golden State Retained a Conditional Asset That Never Matured
sections.body: Golden State received the right to a 2025 second-round selection protected through No. 55, but the condition did not result in a conveyed pick. The club also sent a future protected second to Charlotte, which likewise failed to turn into a selection. Consequently neither franchise can receive credit for a named 2022 or 2025 NBA draft prospect from the trade. The Warriors C grade reflects financial and rotation flexibility after letting a veteran reserve go, without a direct incoming player. The inherited Even Trade verdict recognizes a modest exchange of roster options rather than a balanced flow of on-court scoring. Charlotte received actual Wanamaker games and cash, while Golden State redirected its bench lineup with conditional compensation that never yielded a drafted player. This was an incremental roster move, not a trade involving significant immediate salary or a protected first-rounder.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Even Trade with C grades for Charlotte and Golden State. The Hornets acquired Brad Wanamaker, who played fifteen games as a late-season veteran reserve, plus cash and an unexercised 2022 conditional second. Golden State obtained a protected 2025 second that also never conveyed. Neither team acquired a lasting draft-pick player.

sections.heading: Cleveland Traded Three Young Players and Draft Capital for Mitchell
sections.body: On September 3, 2022, Cleveland completed a blockbuster acquisition of All-Star guard Donovan Mitchell from Utah. The Cavaliers sent Lauri Markkanen, Collin Sexton, rookie Ochai Agbaji and multiple first-round draft assets, although the inherited canonical trade row explicitly lists only the 2025 No. 29 first-round choice alongside the three players. The 2025 selection ultimately was associated with Liam McNeeley. The wider trade also involved additional future picks and swaps whose exact conditions must be tracked in a full source-led ledger reconciliation rather than silently imported into this editorial row. Cleveland wanted a dynamic scorer next to Darius Garland, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen. Utah was beginning a broad rebuild after also trading Rudy Gobert and accepted several younger starters and future flexibility in exchange for its franchise scoring guard.

sections.heading: Mitchell Immediately Produced Elite Cleveland Scoring
sections.body: Mitchell averaged 28.3 points in his first Cavaliers regular season and erupted for 71 points in a January 2023 victory over Chicago, one of the highest single-game totals in league history. He developed into Cleveland’s primary perimeter scorer and helped the club return to the playoffs after several seasons without a LeBron James-led postseason appearance. His ability to attack off the dribble, shoot from deep and create late-clock shots gave the Cavaliers an offensive role none of their other young players filled at the same level. The inherited B+ grade recognizes a highly productive star acquisition while accounting for the exceptional cost in players and future draft capital. Mitchell’s prior Utah postseason numbers belong to the Jazz, but his 2022-23 Cleveland achievements are already sufficient to establish a meaningful return.

sections.heading: Markkanen Emerged as an All-Star in Utah
sections.body: Markkanen was not a salary throw-in. During 2022-23 he averaged 25.6 points and 8.6 rebounds, earned an All-Star selection and won the NBA Most Improved Player award. Utah also gained Sexton as a scoring guard and Agbaji as a developing wing, plus the future first-round capital. That gives the Jazz a direct, substantial basketball return from the three named players, not just speculative draft options. Both sides have B+ inherited grades and an Even Trade verdict, reflecting the fact that Cleveland acquired a prime All-Star guard while Utah received another breakout star and multiple rebuild pieces. The 2025 pick’s eventual NBA career should not be assigned to the Jazz without confirming later rights movement, but the first itself was a real asset.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Even Trade with inherited B+ grades for both Cleveland and Utah. The Cavaliers acquired Donovan Mitchell, who averaged 28.3 points in 2022-23 and scored 71 in one game. Utah obtained All-Star Lauri Markkanen, Collin Sexton, Ochai Agbaji and a future first tied to 2025 No. 29 Liam McNeeley in the canonical record; the larger package includes additional pick conditions requiring reconciliation.

sections.heading: Dallas Acquired Kyrie Irving in Exchange for Two Wings and Picks
sections.body: On February 6, 2023, Brooklyn traded star guard Kyrie Irving and veteran forward Markieff Morris to Dallas for guard Spencer Dinwiddie, forward Dorian Finney-Smith, a future 2027 second-round choice and an unprotected 2029 first-rounder. Irving had spent several productive but turbulent seasons with Brooklyn, where availability and team relationships repeatedly complicated a roster built around Kevin Durant. Dallas wanted another elite shot creator beside Luka Dončić after reaching the 2022 Western Conference Finals. The Nets chose two established NBA rotation players and future draft capital rather than trying to keep a dissatisfied star. The unprotected first is materially different from a conditional second and could be valuable years after the immediate personnel changes. The deal was not Kyrie for Dinwiddie alone.

sections.heading: Irving Became Doncic’s Co-Star and Reached the Finals
sections.body: Irving brought elite ball handling, difficult-shot creation and a second late-game scoring option to Dallas. The first few months were not enough to make the Mavericks playoffs in 2023, but a full offseason and roster adjustments improved their coordination. In 2023-24 Irving averaged 25.6 points, and the Mavericks reached the NBA Finals before losing to Boston. His postseason shot making and offensive partnership with Dončić gave Dallas a direct return that justified acquiring a veteran star despite the initial questions about fit. Irving signed a new contract to stay with the franchise rather than departing after the initial 2023 rental. The inherited A Mavericks grade reflects the prolonged offensive value and Finals run, not merely his pretrade Brooklyn achievements. Morris served a supporting role and should not be assigned equal credit for the team’s scoring.

sections.heading: Brooklyn Obtained Dependable Defense and Future Draft Potential
sections.body: Dinwiddie returned to the Nets as a veteran guard familiar with the organization, while Finney-Smith became a key defensive forward capable of guarding several positions. Brooklyn also held the 2029 unprotected first and a 2027 second, offering future options after its star-driven era came apart. Those were tangible assets, but they did not create another instant Nets title contender. The inherited D grade sharply discounts the immediate on-court replacement for Irving’s elite scoring. Yet the unprotected pick’s eventual outcome is uncertain until the draft, so it would be premature to call the entire Nets return valueless. The Mavericks obtained stronger immediate star production while Brooklyn emphasized longer-term capital and roster stability. These different timelines explain the grade gap without attributing Irving’s Dallas points to Brooklyn.

finalVerdict.heading: Final Verdict
finalVerdict.body: Mavericks Win. Dallas earns A after acquiring Kyrie Irving and Markieff Morris, with Irving providing 25.6 points per game in 2023-24 and helping the franchise reach the NBA Finals. Brooklyn receives D for Spencer Dinwiddie, Dorian Finney-Smith and future 2027 second and unprotected 2029 first-round picks.
